name: Finland
summary: Narcotics Act and Criminal Code ch. 50: using or possessing narcotics is a crime; small amounts usually get summary day-fines. Other psychoactives may be banned from the consumer market (sale illegal, possession not).
callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan law. Health care staff are bound by confidentiality; no specific legal protection for people who call for help.
drugChecking: No established drug checking service found.

lsd.note: Narcotic. Drug use offence: fine or up to 6 months; usually summary day-fines.

mushrooms.note: Psilocybe mushrooms are listed narcotics, and growing them is specifically prohibited.

dmt.note: Narcotic. Since Dec 2022, DMT-containing plant powders and preparations used to get high (e.g. ayahuasca) are listed too.

mescaline.note: Mescaline and mescaline-containing cacti are listed narcotics.

dox.note: DOB, DOM (STP) and DOC are listed narcotics.

5-meo-xxt.note: 5-MeO-DMT is a listed narcotic. 5-MeO-MiPT is not on the narcotics list; it may be banned from sale as a psychoactive substance.

cannabis.note: Narcotic. Possession of about 10 g hash/15 g weed or less usually means 10–20 day-fines. Medical cannabis is very limited.

ketamine.note: Prescription medicine but not on Finland's narcotics list (checked 2026): unprescribed possession isn't a narcotics offence; selling it is illegal.

dxm.note: Explicitly excluded from the narcotics list. Cough medicines with DXM (e.g. Resilar) are sold in pharmacies without prescription.

nitrous.note: Not a narcotic; possession isn't an offence. National sales rules not verified; EU ban on consumer sales expected from Feb 2027.

amphetamines.note: Narcotics. ADHD medicines (lisdexamfetamine, methylphenidate) are legal with a prescription.

mdma.note: Listed narcotic; use and possession are crimes.

cocaine.note: Listed narcotic; use and possession are crimes.

alcohol.note: From 18 for drinks up to 22% ABV (shops sell up to 8%); stronger drinks only at Alko from 20.

ghb/gbl.note: GHB is a listed narcotic. GBL and 1,4-BD are not on the narcotics list (2026). Sodium oxybate is prescription-only.

opioids.note: Heroin and opioid medicines (morphine, oxycodone, fentanyl, buprenorphine) are narcotics; legal only with a prescription.

tramadol.note: Prescription medicine but not on the narcotics list (checked 2026): possession isn't a narcotics offence; unauthorised supply is illegal.

benzodiazepines.note: Listed narcotics (psychotropic list IV): unprescribed possession or use is a drug offence.

maois.note: Medical MAOIs are prescription-only; harmala/Syrian rue aren't listed. DMT plant preparations (ayahuasca) are narcotics.

ssris.note: Prescription-only, not narcotics: possession isn't an offence, but unauthorised sale or import is.
